intro: Let's talk about you. Do you work or are you a student?
What do you enjoy most about your studies or your job?

q: Where is your hometown, and what is it like?
What do you like most about the area where you grew up?
Has your hometown changed much in recent years?
Would you like to live there in the future? Why or why not?
Do you enjoy reading? What kind of things do you read?
Do you prefer reading on paper or on a screen?
Did you read a lot when you were a child?
Is there a book that has influenced you?
How often do you use your phone during the day?
Which app could you not live without?
Do you think you spend too much time online?
Is there any technology you find difficult to use?
What do you usually do in your free time?
Do you prefer spending your free time alone or with others?
Has the way you spend your free time changed since you were younger?
Is there a new hobby you would like to try?
What kind of food do you like?
Do you often cook for yourself?
Is there any food you disliked as a child but enjoy now?
Do people in your country usually eat together as a family?
What is the weather usually like where you live?
Which season do you like best, and why?
Does the weather affect your mood?
Do you check the weather forecast often?
What kind of music do you listen to?
When do you usually listen to music?
Have you ever learned to play a musical instrument?
Do you think music is important in children's education?
Do you have a lot of friends or a few close ones?
How do you usually keep in touch with your friends?
What makes someone a good friend?
Is it easy to make new friends at university?
Do you like travelling?
What was the last place you visited?
Do you prefer travelling alone or with other people?
Where would you like to go in the future?
How many hours do you usually sleep?
Do you ever take naps during the day?
What do you do when you cannot sleep?
Do you think students get enough sleep?
Do you enjoy shopping?
Do you prefer shopping online or in shops?
Is there anything you regret buying?
Do you think people buy too many things nowadays?
How long have you been learning English?
What is the most difficult part of learning English for you?
Would you like to learn another language?
Do you think everyone should learn a second language at school?

p2.t: Describe a teacher who has influenced you.
b: what subject he or she taught
and explain why this teacher influenced you
p2.r: Are you still in contact with this teacher?
p3: What qualities make a good teacher?
Do you think teachers will be replaced by technology in the future?
Should teachers be paid more? Why or why not?
How has the role of the teacher changed compared to the past?

p2.t: Describe a book or article that changed the way you think about something.
b: when and why you read it
and explain how it changed your thinking
p2.r: Would you recommend it to your friends?
p3: Why do some people stop reading after they leave school?
Do you think reading on screens is as good as reading on paper?
What can governments do to encourage reading?
Is it important to read the news every day?

p2.t: Describe a time when you had to make a difficult decision.
b: when you had to make it
and explain how you felt about the result
p2.r: Do you usually make decisions quickly?
p3: Do young people today have more choices than their parents had?
Should parents make important decisions for their children?
Why do some people find it hard to make decisions?
Is it better to make decisions alone or with others?

p2.t: Describe a place in your city where you like to spend time.
b: and explain why you like this place
p2.r: Do many other people go there too?
p3: How have cities changed in the last twenty years?
Should cities have more green spaces? Why?
What are the disadvantages of living in a big city?
Who should be responsible for keeping public places clean?

p2.t: Describe a piece of technology that you find very useful.
b: and explain why it is so useful to you
p2.r: Would it be difficult to live without it?
p3: Has technology made people's lives easier or more stressful?
Should children be allowed to use smartphones?
What jobs might disappear because of artificial intelligence?
Do older people find it harder to adapt to new technology?

p2.t: Describe a skill you would like to learn.
b: and explain why you want to learn it
p2.r: Do your friends have this skill?
p3: Which skills are most important for young people today?
Is it better to learn a skill from a teacher or online?
Do schools teach enough practical skills?
Why do some adults stop learning new things?

p2.t: Describe an occasion when you helped someone.
b: and explain how you felt afterwards
p2.r: Do you often help people you don't know?
p3: Why are some people more willing to help others than others?
Should volunteering be compulsory for students?
Do people help each other less in big cities?
How can companies encourage employees to help their communities?

p2.t: Describe an advertisement that you remember well.
b: what product or service it was for
and explain why you remember it
p3: How does advertising influence what people buy?
Should advertising aimed at children be banned?
Are online advertisements more effective than TV ads?
Do you think advertising tells people the truth?

p2.t: Describe a news story that interested you.
b: where you heard or read it
and explain what you think about it now
p2.r: Did you discuss it with anyone?
p3: Why do people trust some news sources more than others?
How can we recognise fake news?
Has social media changed the way people get news?
Should news organisations focus more on good news?

p2.t: Describe a goal you hope to achieve in the next few years.
b: why it is important to you
what you are doing to achieve it
and explain how you will feel if you achieve it
p2.r: Have you told your family about this goal?
p3: Is it important for young people to have long-term goals?
Why do some people give up on their goals?
Does society put too much pressure on young people to succeed?
Is success mainly a result of hard work or luck?

p2.t: Describe a time when you learned something outside the classroom.
b: and explain why this experience was valuable
p2.r: Do you often learn things this way?
p3: Is experience a better teacher than formal education?
Should universities give credit for work experience?
What are the advantages of studying abroad?
How might education change in the next twenty years?

p2.t: Describe a tradition in your country that you enjoy.
b: and explain why you enjoy it
p2.r: Do young people in your country still follow this tradition?
p3: Why do some traditions disappear over time?
Is it important to protect traditional culture?
How does globalisation affect local traditions?
Should schools teach students about traditions?

chat.s: an open, friendly conversation about anything the student wants to talk about
you are an international exchange student who has just met the student on a university campus in Istanbul
you are a friendly barista and later a customer chatting in a busy café
you are a film enthusiast who wants to discuss films and series the student has watched recently
you politely challenge the student's opinions on a debatable topic (e.g. AI in education, social media, city life) so they practise defending a view with reasons and examples
you are an interviewer for an international scholarship programme asking the student about their goals, strengths and experiences
you are a friend planning a weekend trip with the student and discussing options, budgets and preferences
